metadata.title: ICCS 2022 – nacionalni izveštaj o rezultatima međunarodnog istraživanja o građanskom obrazovanju i učestvu u modernom društvu
metadata.venue: Zavod za vrednovanje kvaliteta obrazovanja i vaspitanja (Beograd)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: ICCS 2022 in Serbia used a nationally representative, multi-stage sampling design with stratification by region (Belgrade, Central Serbia, Vojvodina), urbanization (city/other), and school hierarchy (main vs. branch schools), with explicit strata and no implicit stratification. The study reports participation thresholds (minimum 85% schools and 85% students within schools, or weighted overall participation 75%) and documents exclusions at school and class levels (e.g., very small schools, schools for students with disabilities, and minority-language schools with specified exceptions). For achievement scaling, the report states that results were processed and scaled for international comparison using IRT procedures; however, it does not specify the exact student weight variable names or whether complex-sample replicate weights were applied in the national reporting. Because this is a national descriptive/reporting document rather than an ML re-analysis, the weighting approach is primarily aligned with ICCS/IEA scaling and participation standards rather than with model-based ML estimation.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a national ICCS 2022 reporting and methodology description focused on IRT-scaled achievement and questionnaire-based indicators, not an empirical ML analysis that requires explicit Plausible Values (PV) handling. ICCS achievement scaling is described using IRT and reference levels, while the report does not document a PV-based workflow (e.g., Rubin combining rules or PV draws) for a student-level predictive model. Missing-data handling is therefore not reported in the sense required for an ML pipeline; the report instead emphasizes participation/exclusion rules and quality assurance procedures for the assessment administration.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Target population was students in Grade 8 (about age 14). Sampling used a nationally representative, multi-stage design: first a representative sample of schools (stratified by region, urbanization, and school hierarchy), then random selection of one or two classes per school (two classes only for schools with >170 students). Students in selected classes were assessed. Exclusions followed ICCS-allowed limits: at school level, very small schools, schools educating students with disabilities and students in minority-language schools were excluded (with exceptions specified for Bosnian-language schools). At class level, classes teaching in minority languages were excluded except Bosnian; students in classes following IOP-2 (individual education plan) were excluded. Participation thresholds were applied (minimum 85% schools and 85% students within schools, or weighted overall participation 75%), and participation/response status was documented for student, teacher, and school questionnaires.

data.outcome_summary: ICCS 2022 in Serbia was implemented as a standardized, multi-stage large-scale assessment of Grade 8 students (about age 14) using paper-based testing in the national cycle. The study administered a cognitive test (141 items; 45 minutes) measuring civic knowledge across four content domains and two cognitive domains, alongside contextual questionnaires for students, teachers, and school directors. The report describes IRT-based scaling and the use of ICCS reference levels (A–D) with reported national mean achievement on the ICCS 2022 scale (Serbia: 464 points; ICCS 2022 average: 508). It also reports extensive descriptive results for gender differences, socioeconomic gradients (e.g., SEI and parental education), and multiple civic engagement/attitude indicators (e.g., environmental concern and expected participation), including participation rates and documented exclusions to ensure comparability. Limitations are that this national report does not present an ML predictive modeling pipeline; therefore, no ML performance metrics, PV-combining procedures, or missing-data imputation strategies for modeling are provided.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is treated as a technical/national reporting document rather than an empirical ML paper. Consequently, there are no ML algorithms, no ML target variables, and no model-based performance metrics to populate. The report provides sampling, administration, and IRT scaling descriptions plus descriptive comparative results across countries and subgroups, which explains the absence of ML-specific fields.
